questions.prompt: Which two groups of micro-organisms are used most often in biotechnology?
questions.explanation: Biotechnology mainly uses tiny living things such as bacteria and fungi (including yeast) to make useful products.

questions.prompt: Yeast, the micro-organism used to make tej, is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. It has a true nucleus, which bacteria do not have.

questions.prompt: How does a yeast cell usually make new yeast cells?
questions.explanation: Yeast reproduces by budding, where a small new cell grows out of the parent cell and then separates.

questions.prompt: When bacteria turn milk into ayib (cheese) and irgo, the milk thickens because the bacteria produce:
questions.explanation: Bacteria break down lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid, which thickens the milk and gives it a sharp, tangy taste.

questions.prompt: The antibiotic penicillin, used to treat bacterial infections, is produced by a:
questions.explanation: Penicillin is made by a mould, which is a type of fungus. It is a modern medical use of biotechnology.

questions.prompt: Bacteria are given the human insulin gene so they make insulin in large factories. What is the main advantage of this for people with diabetes?
options: The insulin is exactly human insulin and can be made in large, pure amounts
The bacteria stop needing any food or sugar
The insulin no longer needs to be stored carefully
People no longer need to take insulin at all
questions.explanation: The inserted human gene makes the bacteria produce exact human insulin in large, pure quantities, giving a reliable supply for patients.

questions.prompt: A farmer feeds cow dung and crop waste into a sealed biogas digester. For the bacteria to make methane, the inside of the digester must be:
options: Full of oxygen and very dry
questions.explanation: Biogas (mostly methane) is made by bacteria that break down waste in anaerobic conditions, so the digester must be sealed to keep oxygen out.

questions.prompt: The passing of characteristics from parents to their children is called:
questions.explanation: Heredity (inheritance) is the passing of features such as eye colour or height from parents to offspring through genes.

questions.prompt: A gene is a short section of DNA. What does a single gene actually do for the cell?
options: It carries the instructions to build one characteristic, such as a protein
It stores food for the cell to use as energy
It controls the temperature of the whole body
It pumps water into and out of the cell
questions.explanation: A gene is a section of DNA that codes for one characteristic, giving the cell instructions to build a particular protein.

questions.prompt: The shape of a DNA molecule is described as a:
questions.explanation: DNA is a double helix, like a ladder twisted into a spiral, with two strands joined by paired bases.

questions.prompt: In DNA, the base guanine (G) always pairs with which other base?
questions.explanation: The fixed base pairing rules are C with G and A with T, so guanine always pairs with cytosine.

questions.prompt: Which task in the body is carried out by mitosis?
options: Making sex cells with half the chromosomes
Healing a cut by making new identical cells
Breaking down food in the gut
questions.explanation: Mitosis makes two identical daughter cells, which is how the body grows and repairs damage such as a wound.

questions.prompt: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a human sperm cell made by meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so a sperm or egg has 23 chromosomes. Fertilisation then restores the full 46.

questions.prompt: A baby is born a girl (XX). Which combination of sex chromosomes did the baby receive from its parents?
options: An X from the mother and an X from the father
A Y from the mother and an X from the father
An X from the mother and a Y from the father
A Y from the mother and a Y from the father
questions.explanation: The mother always gives an X. For a girl (XX), the father must also give an X. A boy would get a Y from the father.

questions.prompt: A group of similar cells working together to do one job is called a:
questions.explanation: Similar cells that work together form a tissue. Tissues then build organs, and organs build systems.

questions.prompt: Which organ removes liquid waste from the blood to make urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys are part of the excretory system and remove liquid wastes from the blood as urine.

questions.prompt: Which structure inside a cell releases energy through respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the 'power stations' of the cell, where aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose.

questions.prompt: Malaria is a communicable disease in many parts of Ethiopia. Which action best helps stop it from spreading?
options: Sleeping under treated bed nets to avoid mosquito bites
questions.explanation: Malaria is spread by mosquito bites, so treated bed nets that keep mosquitoes away are an effective way to prevent its spread.

questions.prompt: Besides water and light, what does a green plant need to make glucose by photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water, with light captured by chlorophyll, to make glucose and oxygen.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide enters a leaf for photosynthesis mainly through tiny holes called:
questions.explanation: Stomata are small holes, mostly on the underside of the leaf, that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

questions.prompt: On a dark night, no photosynthesis happens in a plant. Which process still continues in the plant's cells?
questions.explanation: Plants respire day and night to release energy from glucose. Photosynthesis only happens when there is light.

questions.prompt: A ring of bark (containing phloem) is cut away all around a tree trunk. The leaves stay healthy at first, but the roots slowly starve. This shows that phloem normally carries:
options: Water upward from the roots to the leaves
Dissolved food from the leaves down to the roots
Oxygen gas out of the leaf
questions.explanation: Phloem carries dissolved food (glucose) made in the leaves to the rest of the plant. Cutting it stops food reaching the roots, so they starve.

questions.prompt: A village relies on a nearby forest for firewood. They cut trees much faster than new ones can grow back. Forests are normally a renewable resource, so why is this village's forest still in danger of disappearing?
options: It is being used faster than it can be replaced naturally
Forests are actually a non-renewable resource like coal
Trees never grow back once a branch is cut
Renewable resources can never run out, so it is safe
questions.explanation: A renewable resource only lasts if it is used carefully. Cutting trees faster than they regrow means the forest cannot recover and may disappear.

questions.prompt: Farmers on a steep highland slope build step-like ridges across the hillside to slow rainwater and hold the soil. This soil conservation method is called:
questions.explanation: Building level steps across a slope is called terracing. It slows water running downhill, so less fertile topsoil is washed away.
